findingDetails.title: Live Lane-C fixture gold is omitted from the deprecation inventory and retains retired transport identifiers
findingDetails.evidence: The live public/private fixture loader consumes explicit fixture directories; the central corpus loaded 43 sk_design rows with zero errors and 42 private-gold rows retain retired transport labels or payload fields.
findingDetails.scopeProof: loadFixtures recursively discovers public/private pairs; the full central corpus was loaded and the variant sweep found retired labels in dispatch and alias gold rather than one isolated file.
findingDetails.recommendation: Classify undated central fixtures as live inputs, regenerate stale gold/payload fields after removal, and rerun the explicit fixture benchmark; otherwise list exact paths as historical with a no-consumer proof.

claimAdjudication.claim: The deprecation plan can skip central Lane-C fixture pairs as historical even though explicit benchmark runs consume them as public/private gold, and 42 of 43 loaded sk-design rows retain a retired transport label or payload field.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Read the loader, command/workflow binding, loop-host forwarding, scorer route-gold logic, representative public payload, and private gold; verified the corpus is explicitly consumable, prompts themselves are generic, and the scorer treats the retired mode as a negative label rather than a dereferenced route.
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The corpus may be intended as a frozen historical baseline, but it is undated, tracked under deep-improvement assets, enumerated by the live skill manifest, and the command presents fixture-dir as a benchmark input. A historical decision therefore needs exact-path documentation and a no-consumer proof.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Either regenerate the fixture pairs and prove the explicit post-removal benchmark, or document every exact fixture path as historical and prove no live command/workflow loads it.
